papers.name: Component Group 2 Religion, philosophy and ethics in the modern world (one religion, Components 06 to 10)

topics.name: 06 Christianity: Theme 1 Relationships and families
points: Christian views on the role and purpose of the family; marriage and the marriage ceremony
Same-sex marriage, civil partnership, cohabitation, celibacy, pre-marital sex and contraception
Divorce, annulment and remarriage
Men and women: equality, roles in the family and community, religious upbringing of children
Christian understandings of equality: religion and culture, gender inequality, prejudice and discrimination

topics.name: 06 Christianity: Theme 2 The existence of God
points: The Question of God: nature of God, God as good, the problem of evil and suffering
The nature of reality: design, first cause and moral arguments; the Anthropic principle; soul-making and judgement
Experiencing God: revelation through people, scripture, Jesus, conscience and miracles
Experiencing God: conversion, mystical, charismatic and ecstatic experience; worship and sacraments

topics.name: 06 Christianity: Theme 3 Religion, peace and conflict
points: Violence and conflict: forms of violence and their justification
Just War theory and Holy War
Attitudes to conventional, technological and nuclear warfare; terrorism
Peace and peace making: absolute and conditional pacifism, non-violence and working for peace and justice
Sermon on the Mount teachings on peace
Forgiveness and reconciliation; justice, fairness and social injustice

topics.name: 06 Christianity: Theme 4 Dialogue between religious and non-religious beliefs and attitudes
points: Challenges for religion: Christianity in British public life, secularism, secularisation and humanism
Clashes between religious and secular values (education, marriage, equality, medical ethics)
Dialogue within and between religious groups: exclusivism, inclusivism and pluralism; inter-faith dialogue
Religion, national identity and proselytisation
Dialogue with non-religious groups: shared values and disagreements with atheism, agnosticism, humanism and secularism
